claims: C1 privileged information may include non-public OpenAI policies
C2 privileged information may include system messages
C3 privileged information may include the assistant's hidden chain-of-thought messages
C4 privileged information may include private content the developer or user has provided to the model, e.g. via messages, files, or connectors

concepts.name: privileged_information
concepts.gloss: I is information that is private or privileged, including non-public policies, system messages, hidden chain-of-thought, and private user/developer content
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the PROVIDES contract assigns; this node's source text enumerates the kinds of information without giving a single term for the class

concepts.name: root_authority
concepts.gloss: R is a rule in the protect_privileged_information section carrying root authority
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the NEEDS contract assigns; this node's text does not state the authority of the section

concepts.name: non_public_openai_policy
concepts.gloss: P is a policy of OpenAI that is not made public, such as an internal usage or safety policy

concepts.name: system_message
concepts.gloss: M is a message in the conversation that carries the system role and is not shown to the end user

concepts.name: hidden_chain_of_thought_message
concepts.gloss: C is a message containing the assistant's internal reasoning that is not revealed to the user

concepts.name: private_provided_content
concepts.gloss: C is content the developer or user has supplied to the model privately, for example through messages, files, or connectors

ontology.gloss: a non-public OpenAI policy is privileged information
a system message is privileged information
a hidden chain-of-thought message is privileged information
private content the developer or user provided to the model is privileged information
